name: Wide-Grip Barbell Bench Press
description: The Wide-Grip Bench Press uses a hand placement significantly wider than shoulder-width, reducing the bar travel distance and shortening the range of motion at the elbow. This grip places greater mechanical advantage on the pectorals and shifts some load away from the triceps, making it a useful variation for chest-dominant pressing development.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench under the bar. Grip the bar with hands placed 2-4 inches wider than your standard grip on each side, outside the smooth center knurling.
execution.setup_instructions: Position on the bench with shoulder blades retracted and depressed. Grip the bar in a full grip (thumb wrapped). Ensure forearms are vertical when the bar touches the chest.
steps: Step 1: Unrack and hold the bar at arm's length above the chest.
Step 2: Lower the bar under control to touch the lower sternum.
Step 3: Press back to the starting position.
Step 4: Keep the elbows at approximately 70-80 degrees from the torso — wider grip naturally increases elbow flare.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before lowering. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Gripping excessively wide, which places severe strain on the shoulder joint
Allowing the wrists to bend backward under load
safety_considerations: Very wide grip significantly increases shoulder joint stress — do not exceed a grip where forearms are vertical at the bottom
Shoulder pain is a common complaint; reduce grip width immediately if it occurs
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full touch to chest at bottom; full elbow extension at top. ROM is slightly shorter than standard due to wider grip.
coaching_cues: Forearms vertical at the bottom — that is the widest safe grip
Squeeze the bar like you are trying to break it in half
